title: Adaptive quantization-escape vectorizer and attention-tile converter
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: Dequant/cast operations and per-layer precision switching are a significant tail-latency source for realtime decode workloads. Existing kernel selector often flips between precision paths mid-sequence, which induces repeated dequantization and memory traffic. Attention tiling kernels are optimized for a single precision layout and suffer expensive copies when used with mixed-precision KV caches.

Goal: Implement an adaptive "quantization-escape vectorizer" that groups and coalesces dequant/cast work into batched, vectorized micro-ops and a companion "attention-tile converter" that emits attention microkernels compatible with both INT8 and FP8 layouts without repeated full-width casts. Together these should reduce decode 95th/99th tail latency and token-level CPU/GPU overhead for mixed-precision paths while preserving model quality and fallback correctness.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile token latency reduced by >= 12% on streaming decode workloads with INT8 primary path and FP8 fallback
End-to-end throughput for mixed-precision workloads improves by >= 8% under production microbatch distribution
No regression in generation quality (<= 0.5% change in evaluation BLEU/ROUGE or model-specific metric across benchmark prompts)
Canary rollout with auto-fallback succeeds (no increased error rate or SLA breaches over 24h)
approach: 1) Profiling: Extend kernel telemetry to attribute per-layer dequant time, memory copies, and cache misses. 2) Cost model: Build a lightweight runtime estimator that predicts amortized cost of precision switch vs keep-for-layer based on sequence length, batch shape, and KV reuse. 3) Vectorizer: Implement a pass that scans an execution plan and pulls consecutive dequant/cast ops into a single batched GPU kernel (minimizing read/write cycles). 4) Attention-tile converter: Produce tiled attention kernels that accept compact INT8/FP8 packed inputs and emit KV in a hybrid layout to avoid per-token conversions during decode. 5) Prefill/initialization scheduling: Overlap KV warmup with vectorized cast execution and pre-schedule attention-tile transform for the next N tokens to hide dequant overhead. 6) Fallbacks: Add correctness checks and a fast-path to fall back to existing stable kernels on mismatch or numerical anomalies.
tasks: T1: Add microbench harness for per-layer dequant timing (ENG-17211-1)
T2: Implement vectorized cast kernel prototype and unit tests (ENG-17211-2)
T3: Implement attention-tile converter that emits hybrid-layout KV buffers (ENG-17211-3)
T4: Integrate cost model into kernel selector and add runtime flags (ENG-17211-4)
T5: E2E benchmark on production-like traces and quality evals (ENG-17211-5)
T6: Canary rollout and monitor telemetry, then ramp (ENG-17211-6)
notes: We intentionally avoid wholesale replacement of existing kernels; the converter produces adapters that can be JIT-swapped by the selector.
Vectorized cast kernel should support variable vector widths to match different GPU memory alignment constraints.
Focus on minimizing read-after-write memory passes; aim for single-pass dequantization when possible.
Ensure mixed-precision deterministic mode is honored for customers that enable exact-reproducibility flags.
risks: Numerical drift when converting between quant formats — requires regression evals and optional clamp parameters.
Increased register pressure on certain GPUs due to packed hybrid KV layout — might impact occupancy.
Edge cases for very short sequences where vectorization overhead outweighs benefits. Cost model must gate appropriately.
rollout_plan: A: Feature behind flag; internal perf team tests on synthetic and production traces
B: Canary 1% traffic on runtime-1.24 with strict rollback triggers (latency or error spikes)
C: Ramp to 25% if stable for 48h, then 100% with observations for 7 days
D: Post-rollout retrospective and potential QC toggles exposed in Console UI
qa_and_metrics: Instrument token-level latency histograms, per-layer dequant time, and KV copy bandwidth
Track model-quality regressions against canonical prompt set (run nightly)
Add regression threshold alerts to alerting channel #perf-telemetry
